clue.text: Indicate man in field for race

parts.note: to indicate something is to point to it
point is a fielding position in cricket, so the fielder there is called point

explanation.surface: A request to pick out a fielder before a race begins.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, point is a fielder stationed square of the batter on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: A point-to-point is an amateur steeplechase horse race held across farmland in Britain.

clue.text: French old man in residence is decorated

indicators.note: the father is placed inside the home, so this word signals one piece going into another

parts.note: pad is slang for a flat or home
père is French for father, and 'old man' is slang for father

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's father's house has been done up.
explanation.definitionFit: A room decorated with wallpaper has been papered.

clue.text: Foolishly collected in an English city …

parts.note: harvested crops collected are brought in
taken as written
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Someone gathered foolishly in an English city, leading on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something inanely means doing it in a silly, senseless way.

clue.text: … to look carefully in one for conductor

parts.note: taken as written
to scan is to examine closely
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: someone peers inside to find a conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue's surface to 2-down; the wordplay stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian orchestral conductor.

clue.text: It's green — nothing is, around, as can be seen

indicators.note: the words 'is' and 'as' come round the other way in the answer, so this swaps their order

parts.note: nought, the figure for nothing, looks like the letter O
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something green stands with nothing else about it, in plain view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' swaps the order of the two short words; 'as can be seen' also paints a desert green spot with nothing round it.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile, vegetated spot in a desert, the one patch of greenery.

clue.text: Cavort wildly round end of stage, perhaps

definitions.text: Cavort wildly round end of stage, perhaps

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the final letter of stage, enclosing it
letters of the word Cavort are thrown about wildly into a new order
end of means take the final letter of stage

explanation.surface: An actor capers madly about the edge of the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' turns CAVORT into OVRACT, and 'round' puts the E from 'end of stage' inside it; the whole clue also describes hamming it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To overact is to exaggerate a performance, as an actor capering about the stage does.

clue.text: Divine mystic to Holst

explanation.surface: A sacred figure revealed to a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Holst's suite The Planets ends with a movement subtitled 'the Mystic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune is the Roman sea god, and in Holst's orchestral suite The Planets that planet's movement is subtitled the Mystic.

clue.text: Tommy survives drama

parts.note: Tommy Atkins is the traditional name for a British private soldier
to survive is to live on, so survives gives lives

explanation.surface: A soldier comes through a theatrical crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Private Lives is a 1930 comedy play by Noël Coward.

clue.text: Reviewed TV programmes

parts.note: read 'Reviewed' as re-viewed: shows broadcast again so they are watched a second time

explanation.surface: Critics have written up some television shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reviewed' suggests critics, but it means viewed again.
explanation.definitionFit: Shows broadcast a second time are reruns, watched again by viewers.

clue.text: Jack's place of work at end of 1 ac

explanation.surface: Where Jack works, at the finish of the race in 1 across.
explanation.walkthrough: A steeplejack climbs tall structures; early point-to-point races were run across country towards a distant church spire.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplejack works on church spires, and historic cross-country races finished at a church spire.

clue.text: Current suppliers of fish

parts.note: reads as present-day fishmongers, but means creatures of the fish kind that supply electrical current

explanation.surface: Today's fishmongers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day' but means electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: These South American knifefish can deliver powerful shocks of electricity.

clue.text: Flower girl at start of 21 embraces boy

indicators.note: the girl's name holds the boy's name inside it, as in a hug

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name, and those four letters begin the answer to 21 across
Ben is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A flower seller hugs a young lad at the start of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbena is a garden plant grown for its clusters of small blooms.

clue.text: Degree of eminence somebody measures up to

explanation.surface: Someone's prominence is judged by whether they come up to the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: the height a person reaches when measured.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature means both reputation or standing and a person's natural height.

clue.text: Present without jam

parts.note: the present time, recalling Lewis Carroll's 'jam tomorrow and jam yesterday, but never jam' on the current day

explanation.surface: A gift given with no preserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift but means now; the White Queen in Through the Looking-Glass offers jam every other day but never on this one.
explanation.definitionFit: The present day is this day, the one the White Queen says never has jam.

clue.text: Job description? Certainly not

parts.note: the patient biblical Job would describe himself as long-suffering; the opposite trait is meant

explanation.surface: Asked whether something is a job description, the answer is a firm no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' is the biblical figure famed for patience, not employment; 'I'm patient' would be his self-description, so 'certainly not' gives its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking forbearance is the reverse of the proverbial long-suffering of Job.

clue.text: She's at top after trip with expedition

indicators.note: after a stumble the letters fall into a different order

parts.note: the letters of she's at top are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman reaches the summit after a long journey on an expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' suggests a journey but means speed here; 'after trip' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste means with great speed, and expedition is an old word for promptness.

clue.text: £1 belonging to Wooster, occasionally taken by Jeeves

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra
1 looks like the letter I, and is Roman numeral one
Bertie Wooster is P. G. Wodehouse's hero, so his belongings are Bertie's

explanation.surface: Jeeves sometimes helps himself to a pound of Wooster's money.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeeves, Bertie Wooster's valet in Wodehouse's stories, occasionally takes liberties, overstepping his role.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking liberties means acting with undue freedom, which the valet sometimes does with his employer.

clue.text: .Obstacle between playwright and Rex

parts.note: J. M. Barrie wrote Peter Pan
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Something gets in the way between a dramatist and a king.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier is something that blocks the way, like a fence or hurdle.

clue.text: Reduced in numbers, or exhausted

explanation.surface: A depleted and worn-out group.
explanation.definitionFit: Run down describes a staff or stock that has been cut back, and also a person who is tired and in poor health.

clue.text: Canine tooth about right, one concludes

indicators.note: one comes at the end, concluding the answer
the tooth goes about the letter for right, enclosing it

parts.note: a cog is a tooth on a gearwheel
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A canine tooth sits round to the right, which someone concludes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine tooth' looks like one phrase, but 'Canine' is the definition and 'tooth' is a cog on a gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a small Welsh breed of dog, so a canine.

clue.text: Admit Conservative leader, formerly, with two followers

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: once means at some time in the past
the two letters following C in the alphabet are D and E

explanation.surface: A former Tory leader owns up, flanked by two supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'followers' look like political supporters, but are the letters following C in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede is to acknowledge or grant that something is true.

clue.text: One alters flexibly, being the 'pragmatic type

indicators.note: the letters bend into a new order, flexibly arranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone who changes their mind readily proves to be practical.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist accepts things as they are and deals with them practically.

clue.text: Queen in London museum's portico

indicators.note: the queen is placed inside the museum's initials

parts.note: the V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen stands in the entrance porch of a London museum.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed porch along the outside of a building, much like a portico.

clue.text: Chap in certain condition carried up by porter

indicators.note: the reversed condition sits inside the drink

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale

indicators.note: in a down clue, carried up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A man in a particular state is carried upstairs by a hotel porter.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'carried up' reverses the condition word; porter here is the dark beer, not the hotel worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfie is a man's name, so a chap.

clue.text: Drug obtainable from when ban expires

indicators.note: the answer can be obtained from inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A drug becomes available once a prohibition lapses.
explanation.definitionFit: Henbane is a poisonous plant yielding narcotic alkaloids, used as a drug.

clue.text: Fast bowlers on a bonus?

explanation.surface: Do pace bowlers in cricket get extra pay?
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, spinners are slow bowlers; if fast bowlers are on, the spinners are off.
explanation.definitionFit: When pace bowlers are bowling the slow bowlers are not, and a spin-off is an incidental extra benefit.

clue.text: Such constables, as police, nonetheless unusual

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are set in an unusual order
read as none-less: losing the round letter for nothing

parts.note: the letters of as police, before one is removed

explanation.surface: Some constables, like the regular force, are nevertheless out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' removes O (nothing) from AS POLICE, leaving ASPLICE, which 'unusual' rearranges. Britain's special constables are volunteer part-time police officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Special constables are volunteer police officers in Britain.

clue.text: Farmer's boy before he succeeded

parts.note: George III was nicknamed Farmer George; his son ruled in his stead before inheriting the throne

explanation.surface: A farm lad before he made good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Farmer' is George III, nicknamed Farmer George for his interest in agriculture; his son governed for him from 1811 before becoming George IV.
explanation.definitionFit: The son ruled as regent during his father's madness before succeeding as king.
